### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata`, touching **45** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/metadata/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**35** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json bd439f17fa575f38d810c7d58e6873918924ed9b`.

⛔ **15** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/metadata/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **14** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **16** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json bd439f17fa575f38d810c7d58e6873918924ed9b` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `16445492d6ae0c92a7525a7ecf6872bf20aac02e` — the merge of head `46ee0cd402b1ca1cbbc6fbaad95cafcad2eda2fa` into base `bd439f17fa575f38d810c7d58e6873918924ed9b`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 16445492d6ae0c92a7525a7ecf6872bf20aac02e && git checkout 16445492d6ae0c92a7525a7ecf6872bf20aac02e
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin bd439f17fa575f38d810c7d58e6873918924ed9b 46ee0cd402b1ca1cbbc6fbaad95cafcad2eda2fa && git checkout -B drift-repro bd439f17fa575f38d810c7d58e6873918924ed9b && git merge --no-ff 46ee0cd402b1ca1cbbc6fbaad95cafcad2eda2fa

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json bd439f17fa575f38d810c7d58e6873918924ed9b
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs bd439f17fa575f38d810c7d58e6873918924ed9b` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `7617d8691743325cdd2fbe7431964b58a0827db0`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/metadata/src/metadata-manager.ts, packages/metadata/src/stamp-only-row.ts, packages/metadata/src/loaders/database-loader.ts, packages/metadata/src/loaders/loader-interface.ts, packages/metadata/src/migrations/bind-database-loader-row-packages.ts, packages/metadata/src/migrations/detect-stamp-only-rows.ts, packages/metadata/src/index.ts, packages/metadata/src/migrations/index.ts, .changeset/32985-stamp-only-rows-guard.md + packages/spec/src/contracts/metadata-service.ts (`IMetadataService.unregisterPackage`), packages/objectql/src/metadata-facade.ts

### ① Derived judgments

- **Shape test.** `stampOnlyPackageOf` is true only for a body (flat, or either level of the publish envelope) that carries one `_packageId` and no `packageId` or legacy `package` claim. Combined with the empty-column half at each caller, this is exactly the 17.0.0–18.3.0 boot's signature and the host's own item's shape. They can't be told apart from the row, as the module states.
- **`unregisterPackageWithReport`.** It checks every item's rows across every loader (`stampOnlyRows`, a thrown read propagates) before the first `unregisterAt`, so a failed check removes nothing. Kept items stay in the registry and in every loader, are reported per row (loader, id, `source`), and are logged in one `warn` that names the remedy. `force` restores the old path. `unregisterPackage` keeps its `void` answer, so `IMetadataService`'s signature is untouched (the options argument is class-level, as `MetadataUnregisterOptions` is).
- **Binds.** `bindReadRowPackage` returns before binding a stamp-only row, and `migrateDatabaseLoaderRowPackages` leaves it as `'stamp-only'`. The CONTROL shows a real pre-#32246 legacy row (body `packageId`) still binds. The replayed 18.3.0 database measures this: main bound 12 and deleted 34 of 37, this head binds 0 and deletes 0.
- **`detectStampOnlyRows`** is read-only (`find` only) and gives a history verdict per row (`stamp-added` / `stamped-since-create` / `undetermined`).
- **must-fix M1: the narrowing arm is declared as widening.** At this head, existing callers see changed outcomes on published surfaces:
  1. `MetadataManager.unregisterPackage(P)` (exported, and the implementation of `IMetadataService.unregisterPackage`) keeps items it used to remove: every stamp-only row's item. By the changeset's own account this is also every `DatabaseLoader`-stored item of P of a type not stored per `(package, name)` (`object`, `view`, `app`, `page` …), since those rows never get a column. A host that uninstalls a package through this door now keeps those items registered and stored until it passes `{ force: true }`.
  2. The boot bind and `migrateDatabaseLoaderRowPackages` leave rows unbound that they used to bind, so readers of `package_id` see empty where they saw P.
  No input is refused, but an existing call's effect is reduced. That is the same class I ruled a narrowing on #33314 and #33349 (a changed outcome on a published door for an existing caller), and the direction is not purely additive. Declare `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` (the single arm; AGENTS.md), add `fix(metadata)!` and a **BREAKING** paragraph whose fix is "run `detectStampOnlyRows`, then pass `{ force: true }` once the kept rows are the package's own; a package's `object`/`view`/`app`/`page` items are kept until then", and add one ADR-0087 marker (`not-required (no-migration-prescription)` fits: no row is rewritten, and the repair is by hand and deferred). The changeset's What-moves table and false-positive paragraph already carry the substance. This is a text fix; the code can stay.
- nit N1: `detectStampOnlyRows` reads the whole table (`find(table, {})`) and then one history `find` per candidate row. That's fine for an operator tool run once. If an install has many rows, batching the history read by `(type, name)` would help. Optional.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/metadata: patch` is right for a non-protocol change even with the narrowing arm (AGENTS.md: "a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships `patch` and keeps its BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 disposition"). `Metadata-protocol: none` holds, since nothing an author writes is accepted or refused differently.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **No in-tree runtime caller** of `MetadataManager.unregisterPackage` (objectql's facade has its own). The kept-items effect lands on external hosts (cloud uninstall paths) first. That is why the BREAKING banner matters: it is what such a host reads in the CHANGELOG.
- **Past the ruling.** The guard covers rows of every `source`, not only `'database'`. The reason is that the 17.0.0–18.3.0 boot also stamped other writers' package-less rows. It errs toward keeping, never toward deleting or binding, so I accept it. The seat should note it beside the maintainer's ruling, together with the two scope questions already raised (18.4.0 column-bound rows; narrowing false positives by history).
- Folds #33299's N1 (the order note in `keyedEntryBodies`): doc only.
- CI at this head when read (19:48Z): 12 success, 16 skipped, 20 in progress, none red. The ACCEPT re-reads every check at the landing head.

### ④ Design judgment

The maintainer's guard ruling picks fail-closed: an environment row is never removed or bound to the host by its stamp, at the cost of keeping some of the host's own rows. This implementation follows that to the letter at all three doors. It answers what it kept rather than staying silent, keeps the escape hatch explicit (`force`), and keeps the evidence tool read-only until an install reports a non-zero count. The design holds; only the declaration needs to say that the removal and bind doors now do less.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `46ee0cd402b1ca1cbbc6fbaad95cafcad2eda2fa`
Local-runs: none
Scope: .changeset/32985-stamp-only-rows-guard.md, packages/metadata/src/metadata-manager.ts, packages/metadata/src/stamp-only-row.ts, packages/metadata/src/loaders/database-loader.ts, packages/metadata/src/migrations/bind-database-loader-row-packages.ts + AGENTS.md (changeset declarations)

Delta over my FAIL at `7617d8691743325cdd2fbe7431964b58a0827db0` (comment 6883260484). The diff `7617d869...46ee0cd4` is the changeset only (+6/-2). The code is unchanged.

### ① Derived judgments

- **M1 fixed.** `fix(metadata)!` and `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` (the single arm) now name both narrowed outcomes: `unregisterPackage(P)` keeps stamp-only items until `{ force: true }`, explicitly including every `DatabaseLoader`-stored `object`, `view`, `app` and `page` of P, and the boot bind and the operator migration leave such rows unbound. The additive surface is stated as the widening. The **BREAKING** paragraph addresses a caller of `unregisterPackage` over a `DatabaseLoader` and gives the fix (`detectStampOnlyRows`, then `{ force: true }` / `unregisterPackageWithReport`). There is exactly one `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)` marker, which fits because no row is rewritten. The PR title carries `!`, and the body matches and records the any-source acceptance. The author reports the ADR-0087 and no-major gates pass locally.
- Everything in my first record's ①/④ holds unchanged at this head.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/metadata: patch` with BREAKING banner, right for a non-protocol narrowing (AGENTS.md).

### ③ Boundary flags

- The body now says `Refs #32985` per the seat's ruling. The 18.4.0 column-bound rows go to an immediate follow-up PR.
- The full dogfood battery owed by the narrowing arm was not re-run locally (author), so the merge queue's dogfood gate carries it, and the ACCEPT must see it green.
- N1 (detector N+1 history reads) left as optional.
- The ACCEPT re-reads every check at the landing head.

### ④ Design judgment

Unchanged: fail-closed at all three doors, as the maintainer's ruling asks, with an explicit `force` and a read-only evidence tool. It is now declared as what it is.
